notes: Each eval runs a FULL autonomous dev cycle (discover conventions -> worktree -> spec -> plan -> code -> gate -> commit -> PR), so runs are slow, costly, and mutate the repo. Run against a throwaway copy of the repo and have runs stop at local commit (no remote/PR) unless explicitly testing the PR step. Prefer small, self-contained tasks whose quality gate can run without heavy external services.

evals.prompt: Auto-dev this: reject creation of a record when the requested value isn't in the allowed set for that context. Return a typed/handled error instead of throwing. Take it all the way to a PR.
evals.expected_output: Stage 0 discovers the repo's toolchain and quality gate; a worktree + feature branch; a specification.md with observable acceptance criteria (incl. the rejection behavior and that no default value is assumed) and an implementation-plan.md; an implemented allow-list guard with tests; the project's quality gate green; a commit and PR (or local commit if no remote).

evals.prompt: Run the full dev cycle on this fix: the state machine should reject the illegal transition and surface a handled error instead of allowing it. Plan it, build it, verify it, and open a PR.
evals.expected_output: Two planning artifacts; a guard added to the transition logic with a test proving the illegal transition is rejected; the discovered quality gate green; commit + PR.

evals.prompt: auto-dev: add input validation so an entity created with an out-of-range value is rejected at creation time. Self-contained, take it to a PR.
evals.expected_output: Spec with acceptance criteria (out-of-range rejected, boundary defined as an assumption), implementation plan, implemented validation + tests, quality gate green, commit + PR.
